ps140: 4, Podoben “As one valiant among the martyrs…”

O Michael, supreme commander,* shown forth as a most radiant intercessor before the three-Sunned Godhead,* you cry out, rejoicing with the heavenly hosts:* Holy are You, O Father!* Holy are You, O co-unoriginate Son!* Holy are You also, O Holy Spirit!* One glory, one Kingdom and nature,* one Godhead and power!

Your aspect is fiery, and your beauty wondrous, O Michael, first among angels,* for in your immaterial nature you transcend the ends of the earth,* fulfilling the commandments of the Creator of all,* known in the power of your might, making your church a wellspring of healings,* revered in your holy name.

O You who, as it is written, make Your angels spirits and Your ministers a flame of fire:* amid the ranks of Your archangels, O Lord,* You have shown forth as preeminent Michael, the supreme commander,* who obeys Your behest, O Word,* and with fear utters the thrice-holy hymn to Your glory.

Rejoice with us, all you angelic legions,* for the great supreme commander, your superior and our intercessor,* appearing most wondrously this day in his honoured temple, sanctifies it.* Therefore, chanting as is meet, let us cry aloud to him:* Cover us with the shelter of your wings, O Michael, greatest of the archangels!

Rejoice with us, all you choirs of virgins,* for our intercessor, mediator, protection and great refuge* today on her divine and honoured feast comforts the sorrowful.* Therefore, singing to at length as is meet, let us cry aloud:* Protect us with your divine intercession, O all-pure Lady Theotokos!
aposticha: O supreme commander, as general, champion, and chief of the angels,* from all want and grief, from afflictions and grievous sins* free them that hymn and beseech you with faith, O glorious one,* for you are manifestly immaterial, beholding the Immaterial One,* illumined with the unapproachable light of the Master's glory.* For in His love for mankind He took flesh of the Virgin for our sake,* wishing to save the human race.
